page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 40 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 40 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.4 GB per core. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1439.29 and a multi-core score of 38381.56. Memory performance tests show a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2132.58 GB/sec, which drops to 105.52 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 36.66 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512 and AES, reflected in a Passmark CPU encryption score of 17670.65. For specialized workloads, the instance processes 1928.13 tokens per second for 135M parameter LLM prompt processing and achieves 34.66 million operations per second in Redis SET tests.

The instance offers high compute density and dedicated CPU allocation, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means all storage operations rely on network-attached volumes, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The 2.4 GB per core memory allocation also limits its applicability for large-scale in-memory databases. It is best suited for compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, web serving, multi-threaded decompression, and moderate-scale machine learning inference.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.10xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 40 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor, it includes 96.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.4 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Benchmark data shows a multi-core stress-ng score of 38381.56 and a Passmark CPU score of 34144.54. It delivers 34.66 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 23.2 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. This configuration is tailored for CPU-intensive workloads like software compilation, web serving, and multi-threaded data decompression where dedicated compute resources are required, though memory-bound tasks are limited by the 2.4 GB per core ratio.
